display_title_he: עצומת מאס אפקט הגיעה ל-200,000 חתימות
short_summary: A fan petition to save the Mass Effect franchise has surpassed 200,000 signatures, boosted by the original voice actors and supportive gaming communities.

sources.name: IGN
sources.title: Mass Effect's Commander Shepard Actors, Destiny Community Help #SaveMassEffect Petition Cross 200,000 Signatures

paragraphs: The global gaming community has rallied together in an extraordinary display of solidarity following the sudden and devastating closure of legendary role-playing game developer BioWare. After Electronic Arts announced that the studio would be permanently shut down and development on Mass Effect 5 would be entirely canceled, devoted fans quickly took decisive action. According to recent reports, an online petition launched under the banner of the #SaveMassEffect movement has officially crossed the monumental milestone of 200,000 verified signatures within its very first weekend alone, generating a whirlwind of attention across social media platforms.

This rapid surge in community support was significantly amplified by prominent figures closely tied to the franchise. Jennifer Hale and Mark Meer, the iconic voice actors who portrayed the female and male versions of Commander Shepard across the original trilogy, both took to social media to express their profound dismay over the studio's closure and to champion the fan-led cause. Initially, Hale voiced her sadness regarding BioWare's shutdown after a leaked trailer for the canceled Mass Effect: Universe project surfaced online, admitting she felt weirdly hopeful before donning the #SaveMassEffect hashtag. During an Instagram livestream, she was joined by Mark Meer, who echoed her sentiments by calling the news very sad for BioWare's home location in Edmonton, Alberta, Canada, and the gaming industry as a whole. Hale later shared an imaginative vision of fans coming together to create a Kickstarter, joined by investors and a cool game company, forming a collective to bring Mass Effect back to life. Meer echoed these sentiments in a separate video message, famously encouraging his followers to hold the line, declare that he should go and they should go, and sign the petition to demonstrate the immense significance of the iconic series to Electronic Arts.

Remarkably, the movement has also received unexpected reinforcement from other corners of the gaming industry. Members of the Destiny community, who organized their own large-scale efforts earlier this year when Sony moved to cease development of Destiny 2 content, stepped forward to offer vocal backing, reminding everyone that they share a bond with Mass Effect. Additionally, developer Owlcat Games used the official social media account for its upcoming title, The Expanse: Osiris Reborn, to endorse the petition, drawing direct parallels to how fans successfully saved The Expanse television series in the past and prompting followers to do their part.

While industry revivals of this magnitude remain exceptionally rare, the unwavering dedication displayed by the gaming community highlights the enduring legacy of the franchise. As players continue to examine leaked gameplay details and even discuss potential actions like boycotting EA, the future of the science-fiction universe hangs in uncertainty. For now, however, passionate supporters show absolutely no intention of halting their campaign to give the developers and their creative ideas a meaningful path forward.

facts.fact: The #SaveMassEffect petition crossed 200,000 signatures after Electronic Arts announced the closure of BioWare and the cancellation of Mass Effect 5.
Commander Shepard voice actors Jennifer Hale and Mark Meer both released videos supporting the movement and urging fans to sign the petition.
Members of the Destiny community, who previously organized when Sony ceased development of Destiny 2 content, also lent their support to the petition.
Owlcat Games, developer of The Expanse: Osiris Reborn, used its social media account to encourage followers to sign the petition.
